chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the urine of a weaned boy falling into a well, and he said: "One bucket." I said: The urine of a man? He said: "Forty buckets are drawn from it." Then he said: "If a boy urinates in it, seven buckets are drawn from it." This indicates it.

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ: forty; the number of buckets specified for a man's urine
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a boy; the child whose urine affects the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well; the water source being purified
key_terms.الْفَطِيمِ: weaned; describing the child in the first case
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; the impurity discussed in the ruling
key_terms.دَلْوٌ: a bucket; the unit used for drawing water out
key_terms.سَبْعُ: seven; the number of buckets specified in the later statement
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: it is drawn out; referring to removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well if urine falls into it according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the purification of well water when contaminated by urine. It distinguishes between cases involving a weaned boy, a man, and a boy, specifying the number of buckets to be drawn from the well in each case.
